gate_states.0: stream amplitude along the configured port
gate_states.1: hold stock until a nonzero amplitude is available for a resident carrier
gate_states.2: request release, including emission from an occupied internal state

readouts.occupancy: dot(internal,internal) plus dot(amplitude,amplitude), counting every resident or actual in-flight owner once
readouts.momentum: recoil plus direction times dot(amplitude,amplitude), counting every resident or actual in-flight owner once

assumptions: One carrier at most, one nonzero initial amplitude packet at most, one nonzero gate at most, zero baselines and no ongoing sources.
An emission trigger (gate 2) requires no nonzero initial amplitude packet anywhere, including at the carrier node. This excludes overlap between delayed emission and a separate incoming packet.
The carrier owns an independent internal state. The traveling amplitude belongs to a separate local field; interaction eligibility does not change that ownership.
Amplitudes are empty or one signed transverse basis vector. This chosen finite alphabet does not derive quantization.
Signed exchange uses elementary swap, multiplication by a selector and negation. Absorption adds one fixed directional recoil step; emission subtracts it; occupied exchange leaves recoil unchanged.
Gate state is explicit local control stock without an energy or momentum interpretation. It holds arrivals during a pending transaction and is cleared by the joint atomic commit.
A single predecessor and the one-packet envelope avoid same-mode merging. Arbitrary overlapping packets are unsupported; an arrival can invalidate a frozen nonlinear guard and fault the run.
Global readouts are event-audit diagnostics only and never feed updates. Model ticks and computation delay do not establish proper time.
The carrier is held; recoil is an accounting register with no momentum-to-motion or mass-shell relation.
No spinor statistics, electromagnetic gauge law, QED dynamics, physical photon identification or emergent electron claim is supplied.
